title: Volunteer Firefighter Accused of Killing Woman He Called 'Second Mother', Then Responding to Fire
text:
A volunteer firefighter in Ohio has been arrested and charged with aggravated murder and aggravated arson after allegedly setting a fire that killed a woman he considered a 'second mother'. He reportedly then responded to the scene as part of the firefighting crew tasked with extinguishing the blaze.
A volunteer firefighter from Ohio allegedly lit a fire that killed a woman who acted as a "second mother" to him, then arrived to extinguish the blaze. ANSONIA, Ohio - A volunteer firefighter from Ohio allegedly lit a fire that killed a woman who acted as a "second mother" to him, then arrived with his co-workers to extinguish the blaze.
from the Darke County Sherriff's Office, authorities received a 911 call at 12:29 p.m. on April 10 regarding a house fire. "Fire personnel arrived on the scene to find the house engulfed in fire," the release read. "During firefighting operations, fire personnel discovered the body of a deceased adult female inside the house." The victim was reportedly identified as a resident of the burned home, 50-year-old Ericka Kramer, "based on a high degree of probability." Kramer's cause of death was ruled a homicide, police said. Authorities also announced the arrest of 22-year-old Peyton Beam in connection to the fire and Kramer's death. He was charged with aggravated murder and aggravated arson., Beam was a volunteer firefighter who did farm work for Kramer for seven years, even calling her a "second mother." Prosecutors accused Beam of "executing" Kramer by shooting her twice in the back and twice in the head. They claimed he poured gasoline on Kramer's body and set the house on fire before fleeing the scene. " was called out as a firefighter to respond to this scene," prosecutors said.
